Q: Can this palindrome-with-one-deletion algorithm be improved beyond my current approach? A:

This is a LeedCode problem (link to the problem). The time complexity of your solution is O(n), which is optimal. It's not O(n²) because count is at most 2.

Here is a simplified version:

class Solution:
    def validPalindrome(self, s: str) -> bool:
        i, j = 0, len(s) - 1
        while i < j and s[i] == s[j]:
            i, j = i + 1, j - 1
        t = s[i : j + 1]
        return t[1:] == t[1:][::-1] or t[:-1] == t[:-1][::-1]

Q: Questioning the design of SELECT SCOPE_IDENTITY() A:

For example, let's make a variable that keeps tracking for identity changes for each table, would that not be better?

That's quite easily accomplished with this code:

INSERT INTO dbo.tblGender VALUES ('Male')  -- Line A
DECLARE @GenderIdentity INT = SCOPE_IDENTITY();

INSERT INTO dbo.tblPerson VALUES ('Ibrahim', 'Ib@gmail.com', 1, 27) -- Line B
DECLARE @PersonIdentity INT = SCOPE_IDENTITY();

Question: why was it designed that way and not other way?

Well - what would be your expected behaviour, if you run both lines A and lines B, inserting a row in tblGender and another into tblPerson - what would you expect SELECT SCOPE_IDENTITY() to return in this case??
